name: application-menu-category-tabs
title: Menu Category Tabs
description: Sticky pill-tab strip for restaurant menu categories, swapping the item list below as the active category changes.
useWhen: Showing a restaurant or food-ordering menu split into categories (Starters, Mains, Desserts) with a tab strip to jump between them.
You want the category strip to stay visible (sticky) while the item list below scrolls.
A pill-shaped active state fits your visual language better than an underline tab indicator.
avoidWhen: You're building a generic overflowing tab strip for non-menu content (repo sections, settings panels) — use `tab-overflow-scroller` for that unrelated, underline-style case.
Categories don't need to be sticky — a plain non-sticky tab list is simpler and avoids the added stacking-context complexity.
There's no associated item list to swap — a plain segmented control communicates intent better than tabs with no panel change.
responsiveBehavior: Tab strip scrolls horizontally within its own container if categories overflow the available width, rather than wrapping to a second line or shrinking labels.
accessibility: Tabs use role=tablist/role=tab with aria-selected reflecting the active category, giving assistive tech correct tab-group semantics.
The active tab is distinguished by both a filled background and white text, not color alone, so it remains legible without color vision.
The sticky header uses a backdrop blur over a translucent surface so menu items scrolling beneath it remain distinguishable from the tab strip rather than visually merging.

variants.title: Menu Category Tabs
variants.description: Five categories (Starters, Mains, Salads, Desserts, Drinks) with Starters active, showing three starter items with prices.
accessibility: Switching categories swaps the item list in place rather than navigating away, preserving the user's scroll context within the menu.

variants.title: Menu Category Tabs (Dark)
variants.description: Menu category tabs adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: The sticky header's translucent surface and blur are tuned against the dark background to keep the same legible separation from scrolling content.
